name: Oyunbayar Munkhbat
headline: I grew the cultures by hand. Now I build the models that explain them.
intro: I'm Oyunbayar Munkhbat, and most people call me Yuka. I trained as a biotechnology engineer running Streptomyces fermentations, and I am now completing an MSc in Computer Science and Engineering at the Technical University of Sofia. My work is computational biotechnology: bioprocess modelling, machine learning for biological systems and computer vision for microbial analysis.
now: From January 2027 I join Nora Martin's group at the Centre for Genomic Regulation in Barcelona as a research trainee. I am looking for a PhD or industrial PhD position to follow it.
researchLede: My questions start at the bench: how fast does this strain grow, when does it make product, how many colonies are on this plate. Each project below answers one of them with a model, and the same few methods keep returning.
projectsLede: Finished work, work in progress and research I plan to do next. Open any project for its scientific background, method, figures and code.
pathLede: Four years around fermenters and production labs came first. The computing grew out of data I had generated myself and could not analyse well enough by hand.

contactHeadline: Looking for a PhD student who has run the fermenter and written the model?
contactText: I am open to PhD and industrial PhD positions and research traineeships from mid-2027, especially in digital bioprocess engineering, hybrid mechanistic and machine-learning models, and bioimage analysis.
